title: Marker File Agent Discovery
description:
When a workspace is started, the server shall write an `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` marker file to the workspace root containing the shared host port, all endpoint paths, a machine-readable prompt, and PID. All markers point to the same port; workspace identity is resolved via the `X-Workspace-Path` header. The marker shall be removed when the workspace is stopped.

**Covered by:** `MarkerFileService`, `WorkspaceProcessManager`

criteria.text: Agent-plugin version resolution never fails the marker: the scan of the plugin caches under the user profile (.codex/plugins/cache, .claude/plugins/cache, .grok/installed-plugins) skips any directory it cannot traverse (a link or other reparse point, an untrusted mount point, an inaccessible folder), and that covers each cache root itself and every folder between the user profile and it: a cache root that is a link, or that is reached through a link below the user profile (for example a linked .codex, .codex/plugins, .claude/plugins/cache or .grok), contributes no candidate, the same as a link inside the cache, while a user profile that is itself a link is still scanned; a version file (.version or a plugin manifest) that exists but cannot be read (an IO or access error) yields no version, so resolution goes on to the next file and the next candidate; and resolution falls back to the synced plugin version when nothing yields one. Any other error still propagates. Unit tests take every plugin-version input (the agent plugin-root environment variables, the workspace sibling plugin folder and the user profile caches) from test-owned data, never from the process environment, the machine or the real profile (operator 2026-10-20: "Fix scans in PR 87 (Recommended)", "Fold R3-P3 in first" and "Structural fix, round 4 (Recommended)"; operator 2026-10-21: "Fix both, strengthen ACs", hostile validation round 5 finding R5-F1; IMPL-UNITGREEN-001, triage-report-b0e41c36f93c4c91b1bf2524eb579ef8). The hostile-environment runs are out of scope: they are not part of this criterion or its evidence (operator 2026-10-27: "Get ride of the hostile runs enforcing integration test separation.  I have already stated this once." and "Which I sated last night were out of scope."). Moved from AC-TR-MCP-WS-005-001 (operator 2026-10-29: "Move criteria that are misplaced.  Unit tests are for FR, Integration tests are for TR."); its real file-system binding is AC-TR-MCP-WS-005-002.

title: Desktop Process Launch
description:
The server shall support launching interactive desktop processes from a Windows service (LocalSystem) context using `CreateProcessAsUser` with WTS session token negotiation, enabling Copilot CLI and other GUI/console tools to run on the interactive desktop with stdio pipe redirection or visible console windows.

**Covered by:** `DesktopProcessLauncher`, `NativeMethods`

criteria.text: Code that compares a requested environment with the process environment, such as the explicit deltas a desktop process launch passes on, takes that baseline as an explicit input: its unit contract supplies both maps and proves that equal values are omitted and changed values kept whatever the ambient environment holds (operator 2026-10-29: "Strengthen ACs, fix both (Recommended)"; hostile validation finding R8B-F1; moved from TR-MCP-USECASE-018 AC-006 and TR-MCP-USECASE-019 AC-008, operator 2026-10-29: "Move criteria that are misplaced.  Unit tests are for FR, Integration tests are for TR.").

title: Persist workspace paths with forward slashes and platform tag
description: Operator directive (PLAN-PATHNORM-001, decision D1 2026-10-07: delivered in P1). Persisted workspace paths, storage keys and identity hashes use '/' as the separator for all platforms; the windows: (case-insensitive) / case-sensitive: tag is kept; Windows-origin paths are detected by drive letter (C:/) or UNC (//server/share), not by separator; the UNC leading '//' is preserved; paths are converted to '\' only at OS boundaries that require it (\\?\ long-path prefixes, cmd.exe arguments, native APIs). AC1: C:\Users\example, C:/Users/example and c:/users/EXAMPLE produce one storage key. AC2: \\srv\share\x and //srv/share/x produce one storage key that still starts with //. AC3: Existing stores are converted by the --workspace-path-rekey maintenance command (decisions D5-D7 2026-10-07): after it runs no Windows-shaped workspace value contains a backslash, per-table and per-workspace row counts are unchanged, and foreign keys validate; the server refuses to start against an unconverted store (no dual-key lookup). AC4: Native file operations on Windows receive backslash paths where the OS requires them.

title: YAML Protocol STDIO REPL Host
description:
The server shall provide a YAML-envelope STDIO REPL host that accepts structured commands over standard input, executes operations against workspace services, and returns structured YAML responses over standard output. The REPL host shall support the same trust bootstrap, authentication, and workspace resolution semantics as the HTTP and MCP STDIO transports.


**Technical Implementation:** [TR-MCP-REPL-001](./Technical-Requirements.md#tr-mcp-repl-001) | [TR-MCP-REPL-002](./Technical-Requirements.md#tr-mcp-repl-002) | [Mapping](./TR-per-FR-Mapping.md)

**Covered by:** `QBrainAi.Repl.Core` (`IReplProtocol`, `IYamlEnvelope`, `IYamlSerializer`, `IMarkerFileReader`, `ITrustBootstrapService`, `IAuthRotationHandler`, `IWorkspaceSelector`), `QBrainAi.Repl.Host` (`Program.cs`, `AgentStdioHandler`, `InteractiveHandler`, `ServiceCollectionExtensions`)

criteria.text: A command timeout configured through MCPSERVER_REPL_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (agent stdio requests) or MCPSERVER_REPL_STREAM_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (stream commands) is used only when it is a whole number of seconds from 1 to the largest delay the runtime's cancellation timer accepts (4294967 seconds); any other value (unset, empty, not a number, zero, negative or larger) is ignored and the two-minute default applies, so no request fails and the process does not crash because of the configured value, and the timeout message names the timeout that applied; one parse rule serves both variables (hostile validation round 7: both variables at 2147483647 made 19 REPL unit cases throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException from CancellationTokenSource.CancelAfter; triage-report-c993b9446bb8464ba375f74fabd07dad; operator 2026-10-26: "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval"; moved from TR-MCP-REPL-001 AC-002, operator 2026-10-29: "Move criteria that are misplaced.  Unit tests are for FR, Integration tests are for TR.").

title: REPL Credential Discovery Diagnostics
description:
`qbrain-ai-repl --agent-stdio` shall expose `--workspace-path` and `--marker-file` CLI overrides for credential resolution. When marker discovery fails, the diagnostic message shall enumerate every directory searched and distinguish "marker not found" from "marker signature mismatch". The diagnostic is forwarded into the `QBrainAiClient` and appended to the "Authentication required" exception so callers see the root cause rather than the generic message.

**Covered by:** `MarkerFileClientOptionsResolver.TryResolveWithDiagnostics`, `Program.cs` (`--workspace-path` / `--marker-file`), `McpClientBase.EnsureAuthenticated`

title: Session turns record current plan file and MCP TODO id
description: Every session-log turn SHALL store planFile and todoId. After persist, query/get SHALL return both fields. They are never null in API output. When no plan or TODO is active, the stored value SHALL be the exact sentinel None (case-sensitive). The first persist of a turn SHALL reject omitted, null, empty, or whitespace planFile or todoId. planFile SHALL accept a workspace-relative path, an exact absolute path, or a ~/ home-relative path. .. is rejected. Query SHALL support exact filters on planFile and todoId, and text search SHALL match those fields. Existing rows SHALL be backfilled from turn contents and agent history under ~. Import, transcript ingest, and federation apply SHALL persist a validated pair (None if extraction finds nothing). Children: AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-001, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-002, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-003, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-004, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-005, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-006, AC-FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001-007.

criteria.text: Every session-log turn SHALL store planFile and todoId. After persist, query/get SHALL return both fields. They are never null in API output.
When no plan or TODO is active, the stored value SHALL be the exact sentinel None (case-sensitive).

The first ordinary persist of a turn SHALL reject omitted, null, empty, or whitespace planFile or todoId and insert no turn row. A canceled or cancelled supersession may omit the pair, stores the exact sentinel None for each missing value, and a durable reopen preserves that bounded exception.
planFile SHALL accept a workspace-relative path, an exact absolute path, or a ~/ home-relative path. .. is rejected.
Query SHALL support exact filters on planFile and todoId, and text search SHALL match those fields.
Existing rows SHALL be backfilled from turn contents and agent history under ~. Uncertain results stay None. Invented ids/paths are forbidden.
Import, transcript ingest, and federation apply SHALL persist a validated planFile and todoId (None if extraction finds nothing). Null is never stored.

The agent-history scan under ~ (.grok, .claude, .codex, .cursor) skips any directory it cannot traverse (a link or other reparse point, an untrusted mount point, an inaccessible folder), and that covers each history root itself: a history root that is a link contributes no file, the same as a link inside it, while a home folder that is itself a link is still scanned; the scan never fails a submit or an import; when nothing usable is found the turn keeps None (operator 2026-10-20: "Fix scans in PR 87 (Recommended)"; operator 2026-10-21: "Fix both, strengthen ACs", hostile validation round 5 finding R5-F1; IMPL-UNITGREEN-001, triage-report-b0e41c36f93c4c91b1bf2524eb579ef8). Moved from AC-TR-MCP-SESSIONLOG-006-009 (operator 2026-10-29: "Move criteria that are misplaced.  Unit tests are for FR, Integration tests are for TR."); its real file-system binding is AC-TR-MCP-SESSIONLOG-006-010.

title: InstallOllama provisions Ollama on Windows and Linux
description: The Nuke InstallOllama target provisions the local Ollama service the QuadBrain Ollama integration tests use (FR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002), on Windows and on Linux, idempotently: when a server already answers on localhost:11434 with the required model it changes nothing; otherwise it uses an installed ollama executable (on PATH, or on Windows in Ollama's install folder LocalAppData/Programs/Ollama) or a previous portable install under the test-tools folder, else downloads that operating system's portable release into the test-tools folder (Windows: the windows-amd64 zip; Linux: the linux-amd64 archive), starts the server detached and waits until it answers, and pulls the required model (default gemma4:e4b; QBRAINAI_QUADBRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL or MCP_QUADBRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL overrides) when it is absent.

criteria.text: The target's plan is chosen per operating system: a server that already answers with the required model needs no step; otherwise an installed ollama (on PATH, or on Windows LocalAppData/Programs/Ollama/ollama.exe), else a previous portable install under the test-tools folder (ollama.exe on Windows, bin/ollama on Linux), else a download of that operating system's portable release; the plan then starts the server when it is not answering and pulls the model when it is absent (Build.Tests: OllamaInstallPlanAssertion_AcceptsPerOsPlanAndRejectsWindowsOnlyOrMissingStep, then InstallOllama_Plan_PerOperatingSystem_UsesTheShippedPlanner). The required model is QBRAINAI_QUADBRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL when it holds a non-blank value, else MCP_QUADBRAIN_OLLAMA_MODEL when it does, else gemma4:e4b, chosen by one rule that InstallOllama and QuadBrainOllamaEndpointIntegrationTests both use, proved by a unit contract over explicit inputs (operator 2026-11-02: "Strengthen 5 ACs, fix all 8 (Recommended)"; hostile validation finding R9-F5).
Re-running the target when the server already answers with the required model changes nothing (Build.Tests: InstallOllama_Plan_ServerAnswersWithModel_ChangesNothing over the shipped planner).

On the Linux lab host the target leaves a portable Ollama that OllamaServerFixture's resolver finds (TR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002) and the required model installed, and QuadBrainOllamaEndpointIntegrationTests run (TEST-MCP-QBOLLAMA-001).

notes: Nuke behavior is accountable through TR only (operator ruling 2026-10-10); evidence is Build.Tests, run directly as infrastructure, and the live run of the target. Created 2026-10-15 (operator decision "Approve all three (Recommended)"; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B13, triage-report-680916ed).

title: Forward-slash storage keys, rekey maintenance command and startup guard
description: WorkspaceIdentityPath.NormalizeLexicalPath emits '/' for Windows paths (UNC keeps leading '//'; \\?\ device prefixes stripped to drive or // form); BuildStorageKey becomes windows:C:/WORKSPACES/EXAMPLE style. IsRemoteWindowsPath, IsNormalizedPathWithinRoot and NormalizeLocalAdministrativeShareAlias accept both separators. A ToNativePath helper produces backslash paths only for Win32 CreateFile/GetFinalPathNameByHandle, \\?\ long-path prefixes and cmd.exe arguments. Persisted data is rewritten by an explicit maintenance command --workspace-path-rekey (decision D5, 2026-10-07) modelled on McpDatabaseEncryptionTransitionCommand: required backup unless --dry-run, report with old->new mapping and before/after counts; one transaction per database with foreign keys deferred or suspended and fully re-validated (decision D6: SQLite defer_foreign_keys, SQL Server NOCHECK then WITH CHECK CHECK, PostgreSQL DEFERRABLE + SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED); set-based UPDATE per workspace column from a mapping table limited to Windows-shaped values; C# recomputation of hashed values (federation GlobalWorkspaceId/CanonicalWorkspaceId and hub hash-keyed Workspaces rows, TriageGroups GroupKey/GroupId with repointed children, HandoffIngestionRuns ReplayIdentity); FileGitHubWorkspaceTokenStore keys rewritten. No legacy dual-key lookup (decision D7): a startup guard refuses to start while any Windows-shaped workspace id still contains a backslash. Enrolled proxies are re-enrolled once after deploy (the Windows proxy in the original deployment). Plan: docs/plans/2026-10-07-federation-fixes.md section 4c.

criteria.text: Reuse P1.4 Windows lexical normalization, preserve case, and reject distinct old keys converging before any database mutation.
Apply requires successful verified backup; all database changes and FK validation occur in one transaction; repeat apply is a no-op.
Dry-run inventory and planning run only on a database copy; report mappings, table and workspace counts, and retained manual triage hashes without secrets.
HTTP and STDIO startup refuse legacy Windows workspace ids and point to --workspace-path-rekey.
Recompute only derivable triage, handoff, and federation identities; repoint children; preserve manual triage hashes and rewrite token-store keys with file backup.

notes: P1.5 operator decisions 2026-10-16: Policy A uses existing Windows lexical normalizer including device-prefix stripping and case preservation. Distinct old keys converging abort before mutation. Manual triage keys are SHA-256(workspacePath|manual|random GUID); retain their GroupKey/GroupId because GUID is not stored. Only recompute derived identities verified from persisted inputs. Worktree-only implementation and disposable fixture/copy tests; no live apply, service operations, deploy, or merge. Current task explicitly requests requirements/tests first (red), then implementation.

title: YAML Envelope Protocol
description:
The REPL host SHALL parse incoming STDIO lines as YAML-formatted command envelopes containing `type`, `payload` with method-specific parameters, and optional `correlationId`/`requestId`. Response envelopes SHALL contain `type` (`result`/`error`/`event`), `payload` with result data or error details, and echoed identifiers. Malformed YAML SHALL emit structured error responses rather than crashing the process.

**Covered by:** `McpServer.Repl.Core` (`IYamlEnvelope`, `IYamlSerializer`, `IReplProtocol`)

description:
`MarkerFileClientOptionsResolver.TryResolveWithDiagnostics(workspacePathOverride, markerPathOverride, out options, out error)` returns success/failure plus a human-readable diagnostic. The diagnostic enumerates every directory walked, names the marker file when found, and distinguishes "not found" from "malformed" and "signature mismatch". `FindMarkerFile(startPath, out searchedPaths)` exposes the same path list for callers that want raw enumeration. title: Required planFile and todoId scalars with None sentinel and backfill
description:
Session-log turn storage, DTOs, REST, MCP tools, and plugin wrappers SHALL expose required string fields planFile and todoId. New interactive creates/submits/beginTurn/replace-turn reject omitted, null, or empty values. Accepted planFile values are a workspace-relative path, an exact absolute path, a ~/ home-relative path, or the literal sentinel None. Accepted todoId values are a canonical MCP TODO id, ISSUE-N, or None. An EF migration adds both columns, defaults existing rows to None, then a one-time backfill scans turn contents and agent history under ~. Uncertain extractions remain None. Query/get results SHALL return both fields.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-SESSIONLOGCTX-001; TEST: TEST-MCP-SESSIONLOG-006

title: Marker File Service
description:
`MarkerFileService.WriteMarkerAsync` writes `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` to the workspace root. All markers point to the same shared host port. Uses Handlebars.Net templating with full workspace context. The marker template MUST be loaded from `templates/prompt-templates.yaml` via `PromptTemplateService` (id: `default-marker-prompt`). **CRITICAL**: If the template cannot be loaded (missing file, invalid YAML, or missing ID), the service must log a critical error and shut down the server immediately. Fallback to hardcoded templates is PROHIBITED. The YAML file contains port, `baseUrl`, all endpoint paths, process PID, `startedAt` timestamp, workspace name, per-workspace auth token (`apiKey`), and a machine-readable `prompt` block. Agents should send `X-Workspace-Path` header for workspace targeting.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-018
